content: Even if your symptoms improve after a few days, you should continue taking the medication for the full prescribed duration to ensure the infection is completely treated. Common side effects of this medication include nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, or headache. To reduce nausea, it is recommended to take this medication with food. This medication may cause your urine to appear dark yellow or brown. This is a harmless effect and does not require medical attention. Your doctor has prescribed this medication because they have determined that the benefits to your health outweigh the potential risks of side effects. In rare cases, this medication may cause severe and potentially fatal lung problems. These issues can occur within the first month of treatment or after long-term use, typically six months or longer. Rarely, this medication may also lead to serious and potentially fatal liver disease, blood disorders, or nerve problems. This medication may rarely cause a severe intestinal condition known as Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhea. This condition can occur during treatment or weeks to months after the medication has been discontinued. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection, such as oral or vaginal fungal infections. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are rare. However, if you experience symptoms such as rash, itching, swelling (especially of the face, tongue, or throat), severe dizziness, or trouble breathing, seek immediate medical attention. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. If you are in the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking nitrofurantoin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. Nitrofurantoin may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It should not be used near or at the time of delivery (weeks 38–42 of pregnancy) due to the risk of harm to the newborn, such as a specific blood problem called hemolytic anemia. This medication passes into breast milk and may have undesirable effects on nursing infants less than one month old or infants with a specific genetic condition (G6PD deficiency). Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as specific urine glucose tests, potentially causing false test results. If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it later for another infection unless directed by your doctor. Laboratory and/or medical tests, such as complete blood counts, kidney and liver function tests, and urine cultures, should be performed while you are taking this medication to monitor your progress and check for side effects. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
